title: The Precision Vineyard
subtitle: A Grower's Field Guide to AI, Sensors and Robotics — what to adopt, what to skip, and what it pays back in viticulture
fullTitle: The Precision Vineyard: A Grower's Field Guide to AI, Sensors and Robotics
summary: Which vineyard technology earns its place, which does not, and how to tell the difference before you spend.
description: Precision viticulture is sold hard and explained badly. This field guide goes through the tools a grower is actually offered — sensors, imagery, variable-rate equipment, robotics — and asks the only question that matters: what does it pay back, and over how many seasons?
Written for growers and the people who advise them. No vendor language, and no assumption that newer is better.
contents: What precision viticulture actually promises
Sensors in the vineyard, and what they can and cannot see
Imagery: satellite, drone and on-machine
Variable-rate application, and when the maths works
Robotics and automation on a real block
Disease and pest models
What to adopt first, and what to skip
Working out payback for your own vineyard

title: Seed Quality Control
subtitle: A practical guide to imaging and automation in vegetable seed — from production field to certificate
fullTitle: Seed Quality Control: A practical guide to imaging and automation in vegetable seed
summary: How imaging and automation are used across vegetable seed quality control, from the production field through to certification.
description: Seed quality control is one of the places where machine vision has genuinely earned its keep — purity, vigour, health and germination assessment all now have automated counterparts.

This guide follows a seed lot from the production field to the certificate, covering what can be measured automatically at each step, how reliable it is, and where a trained human eye is still required.
contents: What quality control means in vegetable seed
From production field to certificate: the chain
Imaging systems and what they measure
Purity and varietal identity
Germination and vigour testing
Seed health and pathogen detection
Automation, throughput and error
Standards, certification and what auditors expect

title: Vertical Farming
subtitle: A Guide for Growing Minds
fullTitle: Vertical Farming: A Guide for Growing Minds
summary: An accessible introduction to growing food in stacked, controlled environments — the science, the economics and the honest limits.
description: Vertical farming attracts more excitement than scrutiny. This short book explains how controlled-environment agriculture actually works, what it is genuinely good at, and where the economics stop making sense.
Written for students, curious growers and anyone trying to separate the technology from the pitch.
contents: What vertical farming is, and is not
Light, water and nutrients in a controlled environment
Which crops suit it, and which never will
Energy: the number that decides everything
Automation and monitoring
The economics, honestly
Where it fits in a wider food system
